docs.title: Tobas User Guide
docs.text: Tobas is a flight controller for drones and robotic aircraft, built on model-based design and Linux. Its control system is designed with detailed consideration of each aircraft's structure, enabling precise flight even for aircraft that are difficult to control with conventional flight controllers.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Define the aircraft structure in a dedicated format so the controller accurately accounts for it
  • Improve responsiveness and tracking accuracy through motor speed control
  • Compensate for gravity loads and reaction forces as movable joint angles change
  • Compensate for disturbances such as gusts and ground effect
  • Configure the aircraft and control parameters through a GUI
  • Support ROS 2 with the same interface for simulation and real hardware

docs.title: Improved Control Performance
docs.text:
Tobas makes accurate use of your aircraft's physical properties in its control system, allowing it to deliver better control performance than conventional flight controllers. For example, it takes the following information into account:

  • Mechanical parameters of each rigid link in the aircraft: mass, center of mass, and inertia tensor
  • Battery specifications: cell count, discharge capacity, and discharge rate
  • Motor specifications: KV rating, internal resistance, and number of magnetic poles
  • Propeller specifications: diameter, pitch, thrust coefficient, and reaction torque coefficient

docs.title: More Aircraft Design Options
docs.text:
Tobas defines aircraft structures using UADF (Universal Aircraft Description Format), allowing a wide range of aircraft that are difficult to fly with conventional flight controllers. For example, Tobas supports unconventional configurations such as:

  • Aircraft with a center of mass significantly offset by a payload
  • Aircraft with asymmetrically arranged propellers to keep the camera's field of view clear
  • Aircraft equipped with robotic arms
  • Aircraft equipped with tilt rotors

docs.title: Less Gain Tuning
docs.text: Accurate aircraft modeling allows the translational and rotational dynamics to be expressed in an aircraft-independent form and analyzed in advance. This allows Tobas to provide conservative default gains, so users can generally fly without tuning gains themselves. All parameters can also be adjusted online during flight if necessary.

docs.title: Realistic Simulation
docs.text:
Accounting for aircraft mass properties and propulsion aerodynamics enables realistic physics simulation. This can significantly reduce the cost of testing with real hardware.

You can easily simulate factors that strongly affect flight, such as:

  • Wind (steady wind, turbulence, and gusts)
  • Battery voltage drop
  • ESC current limits
  • Sensor delays and noise
  • Suspended payloads

docs.title: Sensors & Processors
docs.text:
• 6-axis IMU: ISM330DLC | STMicroelectronics
  • Magnetometer: IIS2MDC | STMicroelectronics
  • Barometer: ILPS22QS | STMicroelectronics
  • GNSS Receiver: ZED-F9P | u-blox
  • Voltage/Current Sensor: INA228 | Texas Instruments
  • Main Computer: Raspberry Pi 5
  • I/O Controller: STM32H7A3 | STMicroelectronics

  • Power Module: Molex 2.0mm 6pin

docs.title: Quadcopter
docs.text: A conventional quadcopter built with a DJI F450 frame kit.

docs.title: Hexacopter with Noncoplanar Rotors
docs.text: A hexacopter with all propellers tilted 30 degrees from the horizontal plane. While multicopters with coplanar rotors must change attitude to change position, multicopters with noncoplanar rotors can control position and attitude independently. They can therefore translate while remaining level, or change attitude while hovering. They can also generate horizontal thrust directly, providing high positioning accuracy and strong wind resistance.

docs.title: Active-Tilt Hexacopter
docs.text: A hexacopter whose arms can each rotate 120 degrees in either direction. It can make large attitude changes while hovering. Mounted equipment can be held at any attitude, making it a promising platform for applications such as nondestructive inspection of inclined walls.

docs.title: Drone with a Robotic Arm
docs.text: A tilt hexacopter equipped with a four-axis robotic arm. By dynamically compensating for reaction forces and changes in the center of mass caused by the arm, it keeps its position and attitude within a limited range even during large arm movements.

What Is an RPM Filter?
docs.text: An RPM filter is a notch filter whose center frequencies track the motor's rotational frequency and its harmonics. In drones, particularly multicopters, most IMU vibration comes from the propellers. Making the notch filter's center frequencies follow the rotational speed therefore removes these vibrations effectively.

docs.title: Benefits of the RPM Filter
docs.text:
The main advantage of an RPM filter is its very strong vibration attenuation. A notch filter has zero gain at its center frequency, so ideally it completely eliminates vibrations at that frequency. In practice, center-frequency errors and discretization errors prevent complete elimination, but attenuation is still much greater than with a low-pass filter.

The images below show IMU time-series data and frequency analysis results from an F450 flight. Gray represents raw data, and blue represents filtered data. The left column uses only a low-pass filter (LPF) with a 40 Hz cutoff, while the right column uses only an RPM filter. The LPF attenuates high frequencies, but strong vibrations at the motor's rotational frequency remain. The RPM filter substantially attenuates vibrations at the motor's rotational frequency as well as its second and third harmonics.

Reducing IMU vibration, especially gyro vibration, also reduces motor speed fluctuations. In the images below, blue shows measured speed and red shows target speed. The speed fluctuations are smaller when the notch filter is used. This improves attitude control stability by reducing unwanted forces, and also reduces motor heating and makes the propeller sound smoother.

docs.title: Supported FMUs
docs.text:
The RPM filter is available on the following FMUs:

  • FC2xx

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text: Configure the filter under IMU Filter in the GCS's Param Tuning tool. The following sections describe each parameter, its initial setting, and how to tune it.

docs.title: lowpass_filter/*_cutoff
docs.text: These are the cutoff frequencies of the low-pass filters that are separate from the RPM filter. Start by setting all three to 0 Hz to disable those filters. The RPM filter only attenuates vibrations originating from the motors and propellers. If strong vibrations remain, selectively enable the LPFs as needed.

docs.title: rpm_filter/quality_factor
docs.text: This value determines the sharpness of the notch filter. Higher values produce a sharper notch (narrower bandwidth) with less delay. The default is 0, which disables the filter. Start with 5, which provides a balance between delay and bandwidth. After a test flight, confirm that vibration is attenuated enough that peaks are no longer visible in the FFT. Then increase the value in steps of 1, stopping just before the peaks reappear.

docs.title: rpm_filter/min_center_frequency, rpm_filter/fade_range
docs.text:
These parameters determine the range of center frequencies over which the RPM filter is applied. Let the first parameter be \(f_\mathrm{m}\) and the second be \(f_\mathrm{f}\). The notch filter is applied according to the center frequency \(f_\mathrm{c}\) as follows:

  • \(f_\mathrm{c} \lt f_\mathrm{m}\): Filter disabled
  • \(f_\mathrm{m} \le f_\mathrm{c} \lt f_\mathrm{m} + f_\mathrm{f}\): Transition region (filtering becomes stronger as \(f_\mathrm{c}\) increases)
  • \(f_\mathrm{m} + f_\mathrm{f} \le f_\mathrm{c}\): Filter enabled

The disabled region prevents filtering at low frequencies near the control bandwidth, which could adversely affect responsiveness and stability. The transition region prevents abrupt changes in the overall filter characteristics when the RPM filter switches on or off. For a hovering rotational frequency of \(f_\mathrm{h}\), start with approximately \(f_\mathrm{m}=\frac{f_\mathrm{h}}{2}\) and \(f_\mathrm{f}=\frac{f_\mathrm{h}}{4}\).

docs.title: rpm_filter/lpf_cutoff
docs.text: This is the cutoff frequency of the low-pass filter applied to the RPM filter's center frequency. Motor speed readings from the ESC fluctuate considerably. They are smoothed because using them directly as the center frequency would cause excessive changes in the filter characteristics. The default value works well in most cases.

docs.title: System Architecture
docs.text: This page provides an overview of Tobas's hardware and software architecture.

docs.title: Hardware Architecture
docs.text: The diagram below shows the hardware architecture. Sensor data sent from the HAT over a serial connection is converted into common ROS messages by the Hardware Abstraction Layer (HAL) on the Raspberry Pi, then processed by the flight code running on CPU1-3. Target motor speeds output by the flight code pass through the HAL again and are sent to the motor speed control MCU on the HAT. The calculated throttle commands are sent digitally to the ESCs. An interface node for remote communication runs on CPU0 in a separate process from the flight code. All remote access to the flight controller, including access from a ground station, passes through this node. Separating communication processing onto a different process and CPU core preserves the real-time behavior of the flight code and prevents unexpected behavior.

docs.title: Software Architecture
docs.text: The diagram below shows the software architecture. Sensor data from real hardware or an aircraft in Gazebo is converted into common ROS messages by the HAL. The data is sent to the state estimator, which estimates the aircraft's position, attitude, velocity, and angular velocity. The estimated state is sent to the controller shown with a double border in the diagram, where the target thrust for each propeller is calculated. The target motor speed is calculated from the target thrust using the propeller model. The target speeds pass through the HAL again and are sent to the real aircraft or the aircraft in Gazebo. On real hardware, the motor controller on the MCU calculates the voltage to apply to each motor from its target speed and sends the commands to the ESCs. The physical aircraft models required by the flight and motor controllers come from the Tobas project created in Setup Assistant.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: This page summarizes reported issues and their solutions.

docs.title: 1. The Display Server May Not Be X11
docs.text:
Settings / System / About / System Details shows the display server. Check that it is X11.

If the display server is not X11, for example if it shows Wayland, select your username on the Ubuntu login screen and use the gear icon at the lower right to select the display server as follows:

  • If the options are Ubuntu and Ubuntu on Wayland, select Ubuntu.
  • If the options are Ubuntu on Xorg and Ubuntu, select Ubuntu on Xorg.

docs.title: ROS Communication Between the FC and PC Fails
1. The Firewall May Be Blocking UDP
docs.text:
ROS 2 uses UDP internally for communication across the network, but the firewall may not allow it. Check the firewall status with the following command. If UDP ports in the 7400 range are missing from the allowed port list, this may be the cause.

$ sudo ufw status

Ideally, you should allow only the ports being used. As an initial workaround, disable UFW and restart to restore communication.

$ sudo ufw disable
$ sudo reboot

docs.title: The FC Does Not Run After Writing User Code
docs.text:
A runtime error may have occurred. Log in to the Raspberry Pi via SSH and inspect the console output with journalctl for clues. Use the arrow keys to navigate and press Q to exit.

$ ssh pi@${hostname}.local  # or pi@${ip_address}
$ journalctl -u tobas_real_realtime.service -e  # or tobas_real_interface.service

docs.title: What Is UADF?
docs.text: Universal Aircraft Description Format (UADF), defined by Tobas, extends Universal Robot Description Format (URDF), a widely used format for describing robots, with aircraft-specific elements.

docs.title: What Is URDF?
docs.text: URDF is a format for describing any robot that can be represented as a system of rigid links. It defines each link's mass properties, collision geometry, and visual geometry, along with the joints connecting the links. For details, see urdf | ROS.org.

docs.title: Differences Between UADF and URDF
docs.text: In addition to the URDF joint types, UADF adds the following aircraft-specific joint types.

docs.title: thrust
docs.text:
This joint represents a propulsion unit consisting of a motor and propeller. It is based on URDF's continuous joint, with the following differences:

  • axis: The rotation axis. Thrust is assumed to act along this axis.
  • direction: The rotation direction. Set value to cw or ccw.

Note

A thrust joint must be a terminal joint.

docs.title: cs
docs.text:
This joint represents a control surface on a fixed-wing aircraft. It is based on URDF's revolute joint.

Note

A cs joint must be a terminal joint.

docs.title: tilt
docs.text:
This joint represents the tilting joint of an active tilt rotor. It is based on URDF's revolute joint.

Note

A tilt joint must have one thrust joint connected downstream.

docs.title: Creating a UADF
docs.text:
This section creates a UADF for the DJI F450, the conventional quadcopter used in the tutorial.

URDF can reference mesh and texture files for visualization. Because those files are often distributed together with the URDF, it is convenient to create a dedicated ROS package for each robot. Here, we create a package named tobas_f450_description directly under ~/colcon_ws/src/ and include all required files in it. TobasFlightControl/tobas_f450_description hosts the completed package.

docs.title: ROS Package Structure and Required Files
docs.text:
The tobas_f450_description package has the following structure.

tobas_f450_description/
├── meshes
│   ├── frame.stl
│   ├── phantom3_0945_ccw.stl
│   ├── phantom3_0945_cw.stl
│   └── tobas_fc100.stl
├── urdf
│   └── f450.uadf
├── CMakeLists.txt
└── package.xml

package.xml describes the package and its dependencies. Every ROS package must have exactly one at its root. Since this package does not depend on external packages, it only contains essential elements such as the package name and license.

<package format="3">
    <name>tobas_f450_description</name>
    <version>0.0.0</version>
    <description>A UADF example for the DJI F450.</description>
    <maintainer email="m.dohi@tobas.jp">Masayoshi Dohi</maintainer>
    <license>MIT</license>
    <buildtool_depend>ament_cmake</buildtool_depend>
    <export>
        <build_type>ament_cmake</build_type>
    </export>
</package>

CMakeLists.txt defines how the package is built and installed. Configure it to install meshes, which contains the mesh files, and urdf, which contains the UADF.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.25)
project(tobas_f450_description)
find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
install(DIRECTORY meshes urdf DESTINATION share/${PROJECT_NAME})
ament_package()

docs.title: Writing the UADF
docs.text:
The F450 UADF we create here consists of the following components:

  • An empty root link (required)
  • The main frame, including the motors
  • A battery fixed to the main frame
  • An FMU fixed to the main frame
  • Four propellers

Each component is described as a single rigid link. Connecting the links with appropriate joints forms a single tree structure.

In this example, all links, including the main frame, are attached directly to the root link. The overall tree structure is as follows:

base_link
├──frame
├──battery
├──fmu
├──propeller_0
├──propeller_1
├──propeller_2
└──propeller_3

First, write the URDF root element. The root element must be robot, and it must have a name attribute. All the elements below are written inside this root element.

<robot name="f450">
</robot>

Add an empty root link inside robot. The root link is a conceptual link with no size or mass. Every UADF must have exactly one root link.

  <!-- Base Link (Empty) -->
  <link name="base_link"/>

Fix the main frame to the root link. The mesh file in visual is specified by a path relative to the package. Use package://<package name> to specify paths relative to a ROS package in this way. The collision geometry is approximated by a rectangular box because using a mesh would slow down the simulation. The mass properties in inertial are copied directly from 3D CAD.

  <!-- Main Frame -->
  <joint name="frame_joint" type="fixed">
    <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <parent link="base_link"/>
    <child link="frame"/>
  </joint>
  <link name="frame">
    <inertial>
      <mass value="0.55346"/>
      <origin xyz="0 0 -0.004136" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <inertia ixx="0.008128" ixy="0" ixz="0" iyy="0.008193" iyz="0" izz="0.01597"/>
    </inertial>
    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <mesh filename="package://tobas_f450_description/meshes/frame.stl" scale="1 1 1"/>
      </geometry>
      <material name="black">
        <color rgba="0 0 0 1"/>
      </material>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 -0.03" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.35 0.35 0.06"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>

Add the battery and FMU in the same way as the main frame. Their moments of inertia are calculated assuming that their mass is distributed uniformly in a rectangular box of the same size as their collision geometry. See Moments of Inertia for the calculation methods.

  <!-- Battery -->
  <joint name="battery_joint" type="fixed">
    <origin xyz="0 0 -0.025" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <parent link="base_link"/>
    <child link="battery"/>
  </joint>
  <link name="battery">
    <inertial>
      <mass value="0.376"/>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <inertia ixx="9.024e-05" ixy="0" ixz="0" iyy="0.000770831" iyz="0" izz="0.000824975"/>
    </inertial>
    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.155 0.048 0.024"/>
      </geometry>
      <material name="yellow">
        <color rgba="1 1 0 1"/>
      </material>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.155 0.048 0.024"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>

  <!-- Flight Management Unit -->
  <joint name="fmu_joint" type="fixed">
    <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <parent link="base_link"/>
    <child link="fmu"/>
  </joint>
  <link name="fmu">
    <inertial>
      <mass value="0.16"/>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.014" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <inertia ixx="6.17067e-05" ixy="0" ixz="0" iyy="0.000118453" iyz="0" izz="0.000159253"/>
    </inertial>
    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <mesh filename="package://tobas_f450_description/meshes/tobas_fc100.stl" scale="1 1 1"/>
      </geometry>
      <material name="red">
        <color rgba="1 0 0 1"/>
      </material>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.014" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.09 0.062 0.028"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>

Add a propeller. Set the joint type to the UADF-specific thrust type, axis to the +Z thrust direction (0 0 1), and direction to counterclockwise (ccw). The mesh file in visual is specified by a path relative to the package. The collision geometry is approximated by a cylinder. The moments of inertia in inertial are calculated assuming that the mass is distributed uniformly in a cylinder of the same size as the collision geometry. See Moments of Inertia for the calculation methods.

  <!-- Propeller (0) -->
  <joint name="propeller_0_joint" type="thrust">
    <origin xyz="0.159099 -0.159099 0.0247" rpy="0 0 -0.785398"/>
    <axis xyz="0 0 1"/>
    <parent link="base_link"/>
    <child link="propeller_0"/>
    <direction value="ccw"/>
  </joint>
  <link name="propeller_0">
    <inertial>
      <mass value="0.011"/>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.006" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <inertia ixx="3.9732e-05" ixy="0" ixz="0" iyy="3.9732e-05" iyz="0" izz="7.92e-05"/>
    </inertial>
    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <mesh filename="package://tobas_f450_description/meshes/phantom3_0945_ccw.stl" scale="1 1 1"/>
      </geometry>
      <material name="white">
        <color rgba="1 1 1 1"/>
      </material>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.006" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <cylinder radius="0.12" length="0.012"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>

Add the other three propellers in the same way. Note that each has a different joint origin, rotation direction, and mesh path.

The final UADF is shown below.

<robot name="f450">

  <!-- Base Link (Empty) -->
  <link name="base_link"/>

  <!-- Main Frame -->

    <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>

    </inertial>

docs.title: UADF Examples
docs.text:
The example above creates a UADF for a simple quadcopter, but UADF can describe many other aircraft configurations. This section introduces several more examples.

Unlike the previous example, these use XML macros called XACRO to perform programming-like operations such as:

  • Including other files
  • Defining constants
  • Performing simple numerical calculations
  • Encapsulating repeated operations in functions

XACRO makes XML shorter and easier to understand.

docs.title: Non-Planar Octacopter (TOC8)
docs.text:
An octocopter with eight thrust joints. Each propeller is positioned at a vertex of a cube and points outward.

Before XACRO Expansion 
<robot xmlns:xacro="http://ros.org/wiki/xacro" name="toc8_pt001">

  <!-- Included URDF Files -->
  <xacro:include filename="$(find tobas_description)/urdf/components/common.xacro"/>
  <xacro:include filename="$(find tobas_description)/urdf/components/fmu/tobas_fc100.xacro"/>
  <xacro:include filename="$(find tobas_description)/urdf/components/battery/sigp_6s_1100mah_120c.xacro"/>
  <xacro:include filename="$(find tobas_description)/urdf/components/combo/mt3508_0945.uadf"/>

  <!-- Properties -->
  <xacro:property name="frame_width" value="0.5"/>
  <xacro:property name="motor_offset" value="0.1705"/>
  <xacro:property name="x" value="${motor_offset/sqrt3}"/>
  <xacro:property name="prop_pitch" value="0.95"/>

  <!-- Base Link -->
  <link name="base_link"/>

  <!-- Frame -->
  <joint name="frame_joint" type="fixed">
    <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <parent link="base_link"/>
    <child link="frame"/>
  </joint>
  <link name="frame">
    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <mesh filename="package://toc8_pt001_description/meshes/frame.stl" scale="1 1 1"/>
      </geometry>
      <xacro:insert_block name="black"/>
    </visual>
    <inertial>
      <mass value="0.875668"/>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <inertia ixx="2.731e-2" ixy="-1.176e-5" ixz="2.301e-5" iyy="2.415e-2" iyz="-3.35e-7" izz="2.615e-2"/>
    </inertial>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="${frame_width} ${frame_width} ${frame_width}"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>

  <!-- Flight Controller -->
  <xacro:tobas_fc100 parent="base_link">
    <origin xyz="0 0 0.0425" rpy="0 0 0"/>
  </xacro:tobas_fc100>

  <!-- Battery -->
  <xacro:sigp_6s_1100mah_120c link_name="battery" parent="base_link">
    <origin xyz="0 0 -0.060" rpy="${pi/2} 0 0"/>
  </xacro:sigp_6s_1100mah_120c>

  <!-- Propulsion System -->
  <xacro:mt3508_0945 parent="base_link" index="0" direction="ccw">
    <origin xyz="${x} ${x} ${x}" rpy="0 ${prop_pitch} ${pi/4*1}"/>
  </xacro:mt3508_0945>
  <xacro:mt3508_0945 parent="base_link" index="1" direction="cw">
    <origin xyz="${-x} ${x} ${x}" rpy="0 ${prop_pitch} ${pi/4*3}"/>
  </xacro:mt3508_0945>
  <xacro:mt3508_0945 parent="base_link" index="2" direction="ccw">
    <origin xyz="${-x} ${-x} ${x}" rpy="0 ${prop_pitch} ${pi/4*5}"/>
  </xacro:mt3508_0945>
  <xacro:mt3508_0945 parent="base_link" index="3" direction="cw">
    <origin xyz="${x} ${-x} ${x}" rpy="0 ${prop_pitch} ${pi/4*7}"/>
  </xacro:mt3508_0945>
  <xacro:mt3508_0945 parent="base_link" index="4" direction="cw">
    <origin xyz="${x} ${x} ${-x}" rpy="0 ${pi-prop_pitch} ${pi/4*1}"/>
  </xacro:mt3508_0945>
  <xacro:mt3508_0945 parent="base_link" index="5" direction="ccw">
    <origin xyz="${-x} ${x} ${-x}" rpy="0 ${pi-prop_pitch} ${pi/4*3}"/>
  </xacro:mt3508_0945>
  <xacro:mt3508_0945 parent="base_link" index="6" direction="cw">
    <origin xyz="${-x} ${-x} ${-x}" rpy="0 ${pi-prop_pitch} ${pi/4*5}"/>
  </xacro:mt3508_0945>
  <xacro:mt3508_0945 parent="base_link" index="7" direction="ccw">
    <origin xyz="${x} ${-x} ${-x}" rpy="0 ${pi-prop_pitch} ${pi/4*7}"/>
  </xacro:mt3508_0945>

</robot>

docs.title: Active Tilt Hexacopter (Voliro Like)
docs.text:
A hexacopter with six pairs of thrust and tilt joints.

Before XACRO Expansion 
<robot xmlns:xacro="http://ros.org/wiki/xacro" name="voliro_like_pt003">

  <!-- Included URDF Files -->
  <xacro:include filename="$(find tobas_description)/urdf/components/common.xacro"/>
  <xacro:include filename="$(find tobas_description)/urdf/components/fmu/tobas_fc100.xacro"/>
  <xacro:include filename="$(find tobas_description)/urdf/components/battery/hrb_6s_5000mah_50c.xacro"/>
  <xacro:include filename="$(find tobas_description)/urdf/components/landing_gear/zhizicathy_electric_150.xacro"/>
  <xacro:include filename="$(find voliro_like_pt003_description)/urdf/tmotor_1344.uadf"/>

  <!-- Properties -->
  <xacro:property name="arm_offset" value="0.330"/>

  <!-- Base Link -->
  <link name="base_link"/>

  <!-- Body -->
  <joint name="frame_joint" type="fixed">
    <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <parent link="base_link"/>
    <child link="body"/>
  </joint>
  <link name="body">
    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <mesh filename="package://voliro_like_pt003_description/meshes/body.stl" scale="1 1 1"/>
      </geometry>
      <xacro:insert_block name="white"/>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <mesh filename="package://voliro_like_pt003_description/meshes/body.stl" scale="1 1 1"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
    <inertial>
      <mass value="0.575"/>
      <origin xyz="-0.011 0 0.021" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <inertia ixx="6.800e-3" ixy="-1.818e-5" ixz="-1.767e-4" iyy="7.155e-3" iyz="-9.915e-7" izz="1.333e-2"/>
    </inertial>
  </link>

  <!-- Flight Controller -->
  <xacro:tobas_fc100 parent="base_link">
    <origin xyz="0 0 0.058" rpy="0 0 0"/>
  </xacro:tobas_fc100>

  <!-- Battery -->
  <xacro:hrb_6s_5000mah_50c link_name="battery" parent="base_link">
    <origin xyz="0 0 0.026" rpy="${pi/2} 0 0"/>
  </xacro:hrb_6s_5000mah_50c>

  <!-- Tilt Rotor -->
  <xacro:macro name="tilt_rotor" params="index direction yaw_deg">
    <joint name="arm_${index}_joint" type="tilt">
      <origin xyz="${arm_offset*cos(yaw_deg*deg2rad)} ${arm_offset*sin(yaw_deg*deg2rad)} 0.029" rpy="0 0 ${yaw_deg*deg2rad}"/>
      <axis xyz="1 0 0"/>
      <parent link="base_link"/>
      <child link="arm_${index}"/>

      <!-- 9imod BLS-HV25MG-270 @8.4V: https://ja.aliexpress.com/item/1005007702114246.html -->
      <limit lower="${-135*deg2rad}" upper="${135*deg2rad}" velocity="${60*deg2rad/0.04}" effort="${25*gravity/100}"/>
    </joint>

    <link name="arm_${index}">
      <visual>
        <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 ${pi}"/>
        <geometry>
          <mesh filename="package://voliro_like_pt003_description/meshes/arm.stl" scale="1 1 1"/>
        </geometry>
        <xacro:insert_block name="black"/>
      </visual>
      <collision>
        <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 ${pi}"/>
        <geometry>
          <mesh filename="package://voliro_like_pt003_description/meshes/arm.stl" scale="1 1 1"/>
        </geometry>
      </collision>
      <inertial>
        <mass value="0.224"/>
        <origin xyz="0.025 0 5.736e-3" rpy="0 0 ${pi}"/>
        <inertia ixx="8.806e-5" ixy="0" ixz="-8.840e-5" iyy="3.292e-4" iyz="0" izz="2.949e-4"/>
      </inertial>
    </link>

    <xacro:tmotor_1344 parent="arm_${index}" index="${index}" direction="${direction}">
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.034" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    </xacro:tmotor_1344>
  </xacro:macro>

  <xacro:tilt_rotor index="0" direction="ccw" yaw_deg="30"/>
  <xacro:tilt_rotor index="1" direction="cw" yaw_deg="90"/>
  <xacro:tilt_rotor index="2" direction="ccw" yaw_deg="150"/>
  <xacro:tilt_rotor index="3" direction="cw" yaw_deg="210"/>
  <xacro:tilt_rotor index="4" direction="ccw" yaw_deg="270"/>
  <xacro:tilt_rotor index="5" direction="cw" yaw_deg="330"/>

  <!-- Landing Gear -->
  <xacro:zhizicathy_electric_150 parent="base_link" distance="0.165" max_angle="${55*deg2rad}">
    <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
  </xacro:zhizicathy_electric_150>

</robot>

docs.title: Transformable Multicopter (JSK Hydrus)
docs.text:
A quadcopter with three revolute joints in addition to four thrust joints. Users can freely specify commands for the revolute joints.

Before XACRO Expansion 
<robot xmlns:xacro="http://www.ros.org/wiki/xacro" name="hydrus">

  <!-- basic kinematics model -->
  <xacro:include filename="$(find tobas_description)/urdf/components/hydrus/common.xacro"/>
  <xacro:include filename="$(find tobas_description)/urdf/components/hydrus/link.uadf"/>

  <xacro:hydrus_link links="4" self="1" rotor_direction="-1" with_battery="0"/>
  <xacro:hydrus_link links="4" self="2" rotor_direction="1" with_battery="0"/>
  <xacro:hydrus_link links="4" self="3" rotor_direction="-1" with_battery="0"/>
  <xacro:hydrus_link links="4" self="4" rotor_direction="1" with_battery="0"/>

  <!-- special battery arrangement -->
  <xacro:extra_module name="bat1" parent="link1" visible="1" model_url="package://tobas_description/meshes/hydrus/battery/Kypom-3000-6s.dae">
    <origin xyz="${link_length/2} 0.0 -0.048" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <inertial>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <mass value="0.4108"/>
      <inertia ixx="0.0001" iyy="0.0006" izz="0.0006" ixy="0.0" ixz="0.0" iyz="0.0"/>
    </inertial>
  </xacro:extra_module>

  <xacro:extra_module name="bat2" parent="link4" visible="1" model_url="package://tobas_description/meshes/hydrus/battery/Kypom-3000-6s.dae">
    <origin xyz="${link_length/2} 0.0 -0.048" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <inertial>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <mass value="0.4108"/>
      <inertia ixx="0.0001" iyy="0.0006" izz="0.0006" ixy="0.0" ixz="0.0" iyz="0.0"/>
    </inertial>
  </xacro:extra_module>

  <!-- onboard -->
  <!-- 1.  processor -->
  <!-- 1.1 flight controller -->
  <xacro:extra_module name="fc" parent="link2" visible="1" model_url="package://tobas_description/meshes/hydrus/ver2/flight_controller/spinal.dae">    <!-- same with intel euclid -->
    <origin xyz="${link_length / 2 + 0.2221} ${-4.4*0.001} 0.02135" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <inertial>
      <mass value="0.05"/>
      <origin xyz="${13*0.001} ${4.4*0.001} ${-9*0.001}" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <inertia ixx="0.00001" ixy="0.0" ixz="0.0" iyy="0.00001" iyz="0.0" izz="0.00002"/>
    </inertial>
  </xacro:extra_module>
  <!-- end: flight controller -->

  <!-- 1.2 processor: jetson tx2 -->
  <!-- confirm the inertial parameter with real machine -->
  <xacro:extra_module name="pc" parent="link3" visible="1" model_url="package://tobas_description/meshes/hydrus/ver2/processor/jetson_tx2_unit.dae">
    <origin xyz="${link_length / 2 - 0.23775} 0.0 ${-0.01}" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <inertial>
      <mass value="0.181"/>
      <origin xyz="${18 * 0.001} ${4 * 0.001} ${-18 * 0.001}" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <inertia ixx="0.00007" ixy="0.0" ixz="0.0" iyy="0.00003" iyz="0.0" izz="0.00009"/>
    </inertial>
  </xacro:extra_module>
  <!-- end: processor: jetson tx2 -->

  <!-- 2.  sensor -->
  <!-- 2.1 leddar one -->
  <xacro:extra_module name="leddarone" parent="link3" visible="1" model_url="package://tobas_description/meshes/hydrus/sensor/leddar_one_tx2_attached_mode.dae">
    <origin xyz="${link_length/2 - 0.1855} 0.0 -0.0626" rpy="${pi} 0 0"/>
    <inertial>
      <origin xyz="-0.008 0.0 0.0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <mass value="0.025"/>
      <inertia ixx="0.00001" iyy="0.000006" izz="0.00001" ixy="0.000000" ixz="0.000000" iyz="0.000000"/>
    </inertial>
  </xacro:extra_module>
  <!-- end: leddar one -->

  <!-- 2.2 gps -->
  <xacro:extra_module name="gps" parent="link2" visible="1" model_url="package://tobas_description/meshes/hydrus/sensor/gps_ublox_m8n.dae">
    <origin xyz="${link_length/2 + 0.1925} 0.0 0.152" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <inertial>
      <origin xyz="0.000000 0.000000 -0.013" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <mass value="0.042"/>
      <inertia ixx="0.00006" iyy="0.00006" izz="0.000007" ixy="0.000000" ixz="0.000000" iyz="0.000000"/>
    </inertial>
  </xacro:extra_module>
  <xacro:extra_module name="magnet" parent="gps">
    <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <inertial>
      <mass value="0.00001"/>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <inertia ixx="0.000001" ixy="0.0" ixz="0.0" iyy="0.000001" iyz="0.0" izz="0.000002"/>
    </inertial>
  </xacro:extra_module>
  <!-- end: gps -->

</robot>

docs.title: ROS API
docs.text: This page covers only the main APIs, rather than every available API. For details, inspect the running system with commands such as $ ros2 topic list. Use the APIs in the remote_interface namespace to communicate with the FC from an external device.

docs.title: Common
docs.text: These topics are available on both real hardware and in simulation.

docs.title: battery (tobas_msgs/Battery)
docs.text:

std_msgs/Header header

        uint32 nanosec

float64 voltage  # [V]
float64 current  # [A]

docs.title: gnss (tobas_msgs/Gnss)
docs.text:
Position and velocity from GNSS.

std_msgs/Header header
    builtin_interfaces/Time stamp
        int32 sec
        uint32 nanosec
    string frame_id

# Fix Type: gpsFix (UBX-STATUS), fixType (UBX-PVT)
uint8 fix_type
uint8 NO_FIX = 0
uint8 DEAD_RECHONING_ONLY = 1
uint8 FIX_2D = 2
uint8 FIX_3D = 3
uint8 GPS_DEAD_RECHONING_COMBINED = 4
uint8 TIME_ONLY_FIX = 5

# Position
float64 latitude                               # Geodetic latitude [deg]
float64 longitude                              # Geodetic longitude [deg]
float64 height_wgs84                           # Height above the WGS 84 ellipsoid [m]
float64 height_msl                             # Height above mean sea level [m]
tobas_eigen_msgs/Matrix3d position_covariance  # Position covariance [m^2]
    float64[9] data

# Velocity
tobas_kdl_msgs/Vector ground_speed             # Ground velocity in ENU coordinates [m/s]
    float64 x
    float64 y
    float64 z
tobas_eigen_msgs/Matrix3d velocity_covariance  # Ground-velocity covariance [m^2/s^2]
    float64[9] data

# Status
uint8 num_satellites_used  # Satellites used in the navigation solution

                float64 x

            tobas_kdl_msgs/Vector angular
                float64 x

docs.title: User Code (C++)
docs.text:
This section assumes you know the basics of C++ and ROS 2. To learn ROS 2, see Tutorials | ROS 2 Documentation for tutorials.

Among the ROS packages in a Tobas project created with Setup Assistant (e.g., tobas_f450.TBS), the user C++ package (e.g., tobas_f450_user_cpp) is a C++ package you can freely edit. It contains the following five launch files:

  • common_(interface/realtime).launch.py: Runs on both real hardware and in simulation.
  • real_(interface/realtime).launch.py: Runs only on real hardware.
  • gazebo.launch.py: Runs only in simulation.

Both common and real have interface and realtime launch files. Nodes started by the former can communicate over the network via ROS, while nodes started by the latter cannot. For nodes started by *_realtime.launch to communicate over the network, they must go through an interface node started by *_interface.launch. This arrangement prevents the node discovery algorithm in DDS, the ROS 2 backend, from adversely affecting real-time performance.

As an example, create a C++ node that checks GNSS status and publishes a message once per second when a 3D fix is available. Edit tobas_f450_user_cpp/nodes/user_node.cpp as follows.

#include <tobas_constants/ros_interface.hpp>
#include <tobas_node/node.hpp>

#include <tobas_msgs_adapter/gnss.hpp>

class UserNode : public tobas::BaseNode
{
  using self = UserNode;
  using super = tobas::BaseNode;

public:
  explicit UserNode(const rclcpp::NodeOptions& options = rclcpp::NodeOptions());

private:
  tobas::ros2::SubscriberPtr<tobas_msgs::Gnss> gnss_sub_;

  void gnssCb(const tobas_msgs::Gnss::ConstSharedPtr& gnss);
};

UserNode::UserNode(const rclcpp::NodeOptions& options)
  : super("gnss_state_checker", nodeOptions_Default(options))
{
  gnss_sub_ = createSubscriber<tobas_msgs::Gnss>(tobas::topic::kGnss, &self::gnssCb, this);
}

void UserNode::gnssCb(const tobas_msgs::Gnss::ConstSharedPtr& gnss)
{
  if (gnss->fix_type == tobas_msgs::msg::Gnss::FIX_3D) {
    TOBAS_INFO_THROTTLE(1., "GNSS 3D Fix");
  }
}

RCLCPP_COMPONENTS_REGISTER_NODE(UserNode)

Add the dependencies used by this node to tobas_f450_user_cpp/package.xml.

<depend>tobas_constants</depend>
<depend>tobas_node</depend>
<depend>tobas_msgs_adapter</depend>

Add the node to the build targets. Add the dependencies to tobas_f450_user_cpp/CMakeLists.txt and uncomment the build instructions.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.25)
project(tobas_f450_user_cpp)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE AND NOT CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE "Release" CACHE STRING "Build type (default Release)" FORCE)
endif()

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 23)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)
set(CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS "${CMAKE_CXX_FLAGS} -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wshadow -Wswitch-enum -Werror")
set(CMAKE_POSITION_INDEPENDENT_CODE ON)

set(AMENT_DEPENDENCIES
  rclcpp
  rclcpp_components
  tobas_constants
  tobas_node
  tobas_msgs_adapter
)

find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)

foreach(dependency IN ITEMS ${AMENT_DEPENDENCIES})
  find_package(${dependency} REQUIRED)
endforeach()

include_directories(include)

add_library(${PROJECT_NAME} SHARED nodes/user_node.cpp)
ament_target_dependencies(${PROJECT_NAME} ${AMENT_DEPENDENCIES})
target_link_options(${PROJECT_NAME} PRIVATE -Wl,--no-undefined)
rclcpp_components_register_node(${PROJECT_NAME} PLUGIN "UserNode" EXECUTABLE user_node)

install(
  TARGETS ${PROJECT_NAME}
  EXPORT ${PROJECT_NAME}
  LIBRARY DESTINATION lib
  ARCHIVE DESTINATION lib
  RUNTIME DESTINATION bin
  INCLUDES
  DESTINATION include
)

install(DIRECTORY launch DESTINATION share/${PROJECT_NAME})

ament_package()

Configure the node to start automatically. You can start it as a regular ROS node, but here we load it as a component to eliminate copying in topic communication.

Tobas runs three component managers (component_manager_x (x=1,2,3)), each on a separate CPU. Topic communication between their components also uses zero-copy transport. Lower-numbered managers handle faster, more latency-sensitive processing. Their approximate roles are:

  • component_manager_1: IMU filtering, state estimation, attitude/position control, etc. (400-800 Hz)
  • component_manager_2: Path planning, mission execution, etc. (30-100 Hz)
  • component_manager_3: Parameter server, logging, fail-safe processing, etc. (1-10 Hz)

The example node has no strict real-time requirements, so load it into component_manager_3, which handles the slowest processing. Uncomment the add_action section in tobas_f450_user_cpp/launch/common_realtime.launch.py.

# Do not delete or rename this file because it is executed in tobas_f450_config/common_realtime.launch.py.

from launch import LaunchDescription
from launch_ros.actions import LoadComposableNodes
from launch_ros.descriptions import ComposableNode


def generate_launch_description():
    ld = LaunchDescription()

    # Please add the nodes that run both on real hardware and in simulation, with real-time requirements.

    ld.add_action(
        LoadComposableNodes(
            target_container=f"f450/component_manager_3",
            composable_node_descriptions=[
                ComposableNode(
                    package="tobas_f450_user_cpp",
                    plugin="UserNode",
                    extra_arguments=[{"use_intra_process_comms": True}],
                ),
            ],
        )
    )

    return ld

When you start the simulation from the GCS, messages appear in the Control System console.

See ROS API for API details.

docs.title: User Code (Python)
docs.text:
This section assumes you know the basics of Python and ROS 2. To learn ROS 2, see Tutorials | ROS 2 Documentation for tutorials.

Among the ROS packages in a Tobas project created with Setup Assistant (e.g., tobas_f450.TBS), the user Python package (e.g., tobas_f450_user_py) is a Python package you can freely edit. It contains the following three launch files:

  • common.launch.py: Runs on both real hardware and in simulation.
  • real.launch.py: Runs only on real hardware.
  • gazebo.launch.py: Runs only in simulation.

As an example, create a Python node that checks GNSS status and publishes a message when a 3D fix is available. Edit tobas_f450_user_py/tobas_f450_user_py/user_node.py as follows.

import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from rclpy.qos import QoSProfile, ReliabilityPolicy, DurabilityPolicy

from tobas_msgs.msg import Message
from tobas_msgs.msg import Gnss


class UserNode(Node):
    def __init__(self) -> None:
        super().__init__("gnss_state_checker")

        qos = QoSProfile(depth=1)
        qos.reliability = ReliabilityPolicy.BEST_EFFORT
        qos.durability = DurabilityPolicy.VOLATILE

        self._message_pub = self.create_publisher(Message, "message", qos)
        self._gnss_sub = self.create_subscription(Gnss, "gnss", self._gnss_callback, qos)

    def _gnss_callback(self, gnss: Gnss) -> None:
        message = Message()
        message.header.stamp = gnss.header.stamp
        message.name = self.get_name()

        if gnss.fix_type == Gnss.FIX_3D:
            message.level = Message.LEVEL_INFO
            message.message = "GNSS 3D Fix"
            self._message_pub.publish(message)


def main(args=None) -> None:
    rclpy.init(args=args)
    node = UserNode()
    rclpy.spin(node)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

Configure the node to start automatically. Uncomment the add_action section in tobas_f450_user_py/launch/common.launch.py.

# Do not delete or rename this file because it is executed in tobas_f450_config/common_interface.launch.py.

from launch import LaunchDescription
from launch_ros.actions import Node


def generate_launch_description():
    ld = LaunchDescription()

    # Please add the nodes that run both on real hardware and in simulation.

    ld.add_action(
        Node(
            package="tobas_f450_user_py",
            executable="user_node",
        )
    )

    return ld

When you start the simulation from the GCS, messages appear in the Control System console.

See ROS API for API details.

docs.title: Airframe Configuration
docs.text: Use Tobas Setup Assistant to configure your aircraft. Tobas Setup Assistant is a GUI for creating the project folder needed to fly a drone with Tobas. The project folder contains all the information needed for flight, including aircraft mass properties, propeller aerodynamics, and motor electrical characteristics. To use Tobas Setup Assistant, you need a Universal Aircraft Description Format (UADF) file describing your aircraft. For details about UADF, see What is UADF.

docs.title: Preparation
docs.text:
This tutorial uses a DJI F450, a conventional quadcopter. Its components are:

  • Flight controller: Tobas FC201
  • Power module: Tobas PM201
  • Frame: DJI F450 Frame
  • Motors: A2212 920KV (CW x 2, CCW x 2)
  • Propellers: DJI 9450 (CW x 2, CCW x 2)
  • ESC: Flycolor Raptor5 35A x 4
  • Battery: HRB 3S 5000mAh 50C
  • GNSS antenna: TOPGNSS TOP901
  • RC receiver: Futaba R2000SBM

You normally need to create a UADF for your aircraft, but this tutorial uses one that is already provided.

docs.title: Launching the Assistant
docs.text:
Run the following commands in a terminal to launch Tobas Setup Assistant.

$ source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
$ ros2 launch tobas_setup_assistant setup_assistant.launch.py

docs.title: Loading the UADF
docs.text: Click New, select /opt/ros/jazzy/share/tobas_description/urdf/f450.uadf in the file dialog, then click Open. The aircraft appears in the model view and the configuration pages become available.

docs.title: Propulsion System
docs.text: Configure the propulsion system. Since this aircraft is electrically powered, leave Electric Propulsion System checked.

docs.title: Battery
docs.text: Configure the battery. Check the battery specifications and enter the appropriate values in each field.

docs.title: Propulsion Units
docs.text:
Configure each propulsion unit.

Start with the propeller_0 link. Check each component's specifications and enter the appropriate values under ESC, Motor, and Propeller.

Tip

If you are unsure which propeller corresponds to a displayed link name, click the link name in the Frame Tree at the upper left to highlight it in the model view.

Use Aerodynamics to configure the propeller's aerodynamic characteristics. Several configuration methods are available. For the DJI 9450 propeller used here, a predefined model is provided. Select Select Propeller Model from the first list, then select dji_9450 from the list below it.

All four propulsion units on this aircraft are identical, so click Copy To All to copy the propeller_0 settings to the other three units. Confirm that the propeller_0 settings are reflected in the other tabs.

docs.title: Hardware Interface
docs.text:
Configure the hardware connections. Make sure Tobas FC2xx is selected, then assign the appropriate DShot channel to each of the four propulsion units.

Note

If you do not specify an interface here, for example when using CAN ESCs, the hardware will not be driven by the default configuration. You will need to write your own ROS node to connect the hardware to the Tobas software.

docs.title: Remote Connection
docs.text: Configure remote access from the ground station to the FC.

docs.title: Network Interface
docs.text: Specify the network interface the FC uses to communicate with external devices. This tutorial uses a portable Wi-Fi router for communication between the FC and GCS, so select Wireless. Select Wired if you use wired Ethernet. Select Access Point if you use the Raspberry Pi's built-in access point without an external communication module. For other configurations, such as a VPN interface named tun0, select Other and enter the interface name directly.

docs.title: Host
docs.text: Configure the address the GCS uses to identify the FC on the LAN. You can use a static IP address directly if one is configured, but this tutorial uses a hostname for convenience. Select Hostname and enter the FC hostname configured in Boot Device Configuration.

docs.title: Saving the Project
docs.text: Click Save and save the project as tobas_f450.TBS under ~/.local/share/tobas/colcon_ws/src/ in the file dialog.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: Configuration is now complete. Close Setup Assistant. Next, assemble the aircraft and set up the hardware.

docs.title: Boot Device Configuration
docs.text: First, configure the initial communication settings by editing the boot device directly. Prepare the microSD card containing the Tobas image.

docs.title: Launching the Configuration GUI
docs.text:
Run the following command in a terminal to launch Tobas Bootmedia Config. Root privileges are required to work with external volumes.

$ sudo bash -c 'source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash && ros2 run tobas_bootmedia_config TobasBootmediaConfig'

docs.title: Connecting to the Boot Device
docs.text:
Insert the SD card into your PC using a suitable USB card reader. If the Tobas image was flashed correctly, the SD card will be available in the selection list at the top of the GUI.

Make sure the correct SD card is selected, then click Connect. The SD card will be mounted on your PC and the current settings will be loaded.

docs.title: Hostname
docs.text:
Edit the Linux hostname.

By default, Tobas uses hostnames to identify devices on the network, so the hostname must be unique within the subnet you plan to use. You can also use a static IP address, but keeping hostnames unique is a good precaution when operating multiple aircraft at once.

Edit the hostname and click Write to write the new hostname to the SD card.

docs.title: Login Password
docs.text:
Edit the login password.

The default password, tobas, will work, but changing it is recommended for security.

Enter the login password in New Password, then enter it again in Confirm Password. The Write button becomes available when both entries match and the password is valid. Click Write to write the password to the SD card.

docs.title: SSH Keys
docs.text:
Configure SSH key authentication.

Tobas uses SSH key authentication for some operations from the ground station to the flight controller (FC), so you need to register the public key of your ground station PC on the FC.

First, create an SSH key pair. Run the following command in a terminal to launch Passwords and Keys.

$ seahorse

Click the + button in the upper left and select Secure Shell key. In the dialog, enter an identifier such as <username>@<hostname> in Description, then click Generate. Click OK in the next dialog to generate the SSH public and private keys. You can leave the password blank. Click OpenSSH keys to confirm that the newly created key is listed. Double-click the key, copy the Public key from the dialog, then close Passwords and Keys.

Return to Tobas Bootmedia Config, click Add, and paste the public key into the dialog. Click OK to add the public key to the list and write it to the SD card.

docs.title: Wi-Fi Client
docs.text:
Configure the FC to operate as a Wi-Fi client.

Tobas uses ROS 2 (DDS) for remote communication, so all devices that need to communicate, including the FC and ground station, must be on the same subnet. You can skip this section if you only use Ethernet or operate the FC as an access point.

Click Add and enter the SSID and PSK of the access point you want to connect to in the dialog. Priority determines the connection priority. When multiple networks are available, higher values take precedence. Click OK to add the access point to the table and write it to the SD card.

docs.title: Wi-Fi Hotspot
docs.text:
Configure the FC to operate as a Wi-Fi access point.

As described above, the FC and ground station must be on the same subnet to communicate. Using the FC itself as an access point is convenient for outdoor flight tests because it eliminates the need for an external router. You can skip this section if the FC will only operate as a Wi-Fi client.

Enter your chosen SSID and PSK in New SSID and New PSK, respectively. The Write button becomes available when both values are valid. Click Write to write the SSID and PSK to the SD card.

docs.title: Finishing Up
docs.text: Once configuration is complete, click Disconnect. The boot device will be unmounted and can be safely removed. Close the GUI and remove the SD card from your PC.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: Configuration is now complete. Next, use Tobas Setup Assistant to create your first project.

docs.title: Starting
docs.text:
1. Connect power to the aircraft.
  2. Launch Tobas GCS.
  3. Click Load Project and load tobas_f450.TBS.
  4. Click the Control System tool button to open it.
  5. Make sure the pre-arm safety checks pass and Ready to Arm appears at the top of the window.
  6. Turn on the RC transmitter, turn the Enable switch on, and turn the Kill switch off.
  7. Select the flight mode using the transmitter switch. Stabilize (attitude control mode) is a safe choice to start with.
  8. Hold the throttle stick down and the yaw stick to the right for one second to arm.
  9. Once armed, center the yaw stick and gradually raise the throttle stick.

Note

In environments where GNSS is unavailable, such as indoors, the position and velocity checks cannot pass. You need to disable those checks in the Fail-Safe tab of Setup Assistant.

docs.title: Stopping
docs.text:
1. Hold the throttle stick down and the yaw stick to the left for one second to disarm. Alternatively, turn the Kill switch on to disarm immediately.
  2. Turn off power to the aircraft, taking all necessary safety precautions.

The following sections describe the ground station's features.

docs.title: Control System
docs.text: Control System is a tool for monitoring drone status and planning missions.

docs.title: Status Monitoring
docs.text:
The left side of the window displays the following status information:

  • Position and attitude: roll, pitch, yaw, and altitude
  • Battery status: voltage and current
  • CPU status: temperature and load
  • GNSS status: receiver status and satellite count
  • RC input: sticks, kill switch, flight mode, and other switches
  • Motor status: speed and communication status for each motor
  • Pre-Arm Check: battery voltage, state estimation accuracy, and other checks
  • Messages from each node

docs.title: Mission Planning
docs.text:
The right side of the window lets you plan and execute flight missions.

  1. Click Add to add commands. The example below plans a mission that takes off, visits eight waypoints, returns to the takeoff point, and lands.
  2. Set the parameters for each command in the dialog at the lower right. You can also change waypoint coordinates by dragging their icons on the map.
  3. Click Execute to run the mission.

Note

Always turn the transmitter's Enable switch off before executing a mission, because transmitter commands take priority when it is on.

docs.title: Param Tuning
docs.text: Param Tuning is a tool for adjusting flight parameters online.

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
1. Click Load to read the current parameters from the FC.
  2. Adjust parameters online using the increment/decrement buttons or sliders.
  3. Click Save to save the current parameters to the project folder on your local PC.
  4. After the flight, click Write Project to flash the saved parameters to the FC.

docs.title: attitude_natural_frequency
docs.text: This parameter controls the responsiveness of attitude control. Higher values produce a faster response to the target attitude, but excessively high values make attitude control unstable. Increase the value gradually while checking that no oscillations occur. For this aircraft, the value could be increased to 25 rad/s.

docs.title: heading_natural_frequency
docs.text: This parameter controls the responsiveness of heading control. Higher values produce a faster response to the target heading, but excessively high values make heading control unstable. Increase the value gradually while checking that no oscillations occur. The default value is used in this example.

docs.title: horizontal_natural_frequency
docs.text: This parameter controls the responsiveness of horizontal position control. Higher values produce a faster response to the target position, but excessively high values make position control unstable. Increase the value gradually while checking that no oscillations occur. The default value is used in this example.

docs.title: vertical_natural_frequency
docs.text: This parameter controls the responsiveness of vertical position control. Higher values produce a faster response to the target altitude, but excessively high values make altitude control unstable. Increase the value gradually while checking that no oscillations occur. The default value is used in this example.

docs.title: lowpass_filter/gyro_cutoff
docs.text:
This is the cutoff frequency of the gyro sensor's low-pass filter. Lower values suppress gyro noise more strongly, but excessively low values introduce signal delay that makes angular velocity control unstable. Check the flight log (described below). If the target motor speed oscillates with an amplitude of 10% or more of the hovering speed, the filtered angular velocity oscillations are too large; reduce this value. The default value is used in this example.

Tip

Some FMUs support an RPM filter that efficiently attenuates propeller vibrations. You can configure it here in the same way as the parameters above. We recommend enabling this powerful feature.

docs.title: Flight Log
docs.text: Flight Log is a tool for recording and replaying aircraft state data during flight.

docs.title: Recording a Flight Log
docs.text:
1. Enter a log name in Log Name (e.g., 20260101_f450_hover).
  2. Click Start Recording to start recording the log.
  3. Click Stop Recording to stop recording.

docs.title: Viewing a Flight Log
docs.text:
1. Click the Read buttons on the FC and PC sides to display the logs stored on each.
  2. Click Download to the right of a log name in the FC list to download that log to your PC.
  3. Click a log name in the PC list to plot the recorded data on the right.
  4. Use the play/stop buttons and slider at the lower right to change the displayed log time.

docs.title: Assembling the Aircraft
docs.text:
Assemble the aircraft according to the configuration you created in Setup Assistant.

Note

Always provide at least basic vibration isolation when mounting the flight controller on the aircraft. An overly rigid mount can transmit motor and propeller vibrations to the accelerometer, reducing attitude estimation accuracy. An overly soft mount can delay the gyro response and cause oscillations in angular velocity control. For easy-to-use mounting materials, we recommend Holybro Foam Pads or Kyosho Z8006B.

docs.title: RC Transmitter Configuration
docs.text:
The S.BUS signal is expected to provide at least eight channels. Tobas assigns the following roles to the RC input channels:

Channel Role Interface CH1 Roll Stick CH2 Pitch Stick CH3 Throttle Stick CH4 Yaw Stick CH5 Flight mode Three-position switch CH6 Sub-flight mode Two-position switch CH7 Enable/disable Two-position switch CH8 Kill Two-position switch CH9-16 GPSw Two-position switch

The sub-flight mode switch selects more specific modes within certain flight modes. It is used when the four basic stick axes do not provide enough command degrees of freedom, such as when switching modes on aircraft capable of controlling five or more axes simultaneously. GPSw (General Purpose Switch) channels are freely available for user-defined purposes. You can set their number in Setup Assistant to suit your transmitter, receiver, and application.

Futaba T10J has fixed assignments for channels 1 through 4 as shown in the table above, while switches can be freely assigned to channels 5 and above. Hold the transmitter's + button to open the menu, then select AUX Channel. The following assignments are used in this tutorial.

Channel Switch CH5 SwE CH6 SwG CH7 SwA CH8 SwC CH9 NULL CH10 NULL

When using a Futaba transmitter, you also need to reverse the throttle stick. Hold the transmitter's + button to open the menu, then select Reverse. Set only the throttle stick (THR) to reverse (REV).

docs.title: Loading and Writing the Tobas Project
docs.text:
Connect your ground station PC to the same network as the FC. If you configured multiple networks in Boot Device Configuration, remember that the available network with the highest priority is selected.

Run the following commands in a terminal to launch Tobas GCS.

$ source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
$ RMW_IMPLEMENTATION=rmw_cyclonedds_cpp ros2 launch tobas_gcs gcs.launch.py

Click Load Project, then double-click the tobas_f450.TBS project created in Setup Assistant to load it.

Click Write Project to send the project to the FC and build it there. This takes a few minutes.

docs.title: Sensor Calibration
docs.text: Calibrate each sensor. Click Sensor Calib among the tool buttons at the top of the window.

docs.title: Accelerometer Calibration
docs.text: Calibrate the accelerometer. Place the aircraft on a level surface and click Start. Calibration completes in a few seconds, and the tab changes from red to green shortly afterward.

docs.title: Magnetometer Calibration
docs.text:
Calibrate the magnetometer. The magnetometer is strongly affected by its surroundings, so perform calibration with the FC mounted on the aircraft. Preferably, choose an area free of magnetic materials such as steel reinforcement.

  1. Click Start to begin displaying magnetometer readings as a white point cloud.
  2. For each of the FC's six faces, hold that face upward and slowly rotate the aircraft about the vertical axis. Calibration is complete when the progress bar reaches 100%.
  3. Click Finish when done. The estimated ellipsoid is shown in blue, and the corrected point cloud is shown in green. Calibration is successful if the blue ellipsoid overlaps the white point cloud and the green point cloud forms a sphere around the origin.

docs.title: Radio Calibration
docs.text:
Calibrate the radio input (S.BUS).

  1. Click Start to begin displaying the values of each S.BUS channel.
  2. Move each stick or switch through its full operating range. If a stick and its GUI bar move in opposite directions, adjust the transmitter settings accordingly.
  3. Click Finish when done.

docs.title: Actuator Test
docs.text: Test each actuator. Click Actuator Test among the tool buttons at the top of the window.

docs.title: Rotor Test
docs.text:
Warning: This operation spins the motors. Use extreme caution if you perform it with propellers attached.

  1. Click Start to enable all motors to spin.
  2. For each motor, move the slider to command its speed and verify that the connection and rotation direction are correct.
  3. Tune each motor's control gain. Increase the gains one at a time while changing the target speed and checking that no oscillations occur. In this example, all gains are set to 17.
  4. Click Save to save the control gains to the project on your PC.
  5. Click Stop to end the test.
  6. Click Write Project to flash the saved control gains to the FC.

Note

If the motors do not spin, check whether the ERR indicator on the top of the FC is lit. If it is lit, try turning the power off and then back on.

docs.title: Joint Test
docs.text: If your aircraft has actuated joints, such as tilt rotors or fixed-wing control surfaces, you can test position commands for each joint. The aircraft in this tutorial has no movable joints other than the propellers, so skip this step.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: Hardware setup is now complete. Close Tobas GCS and turn off the aircraft. In the next step, you will fly the aircraft.

docs.title: Installing ROS 2 Jazzy
docs.text: Follow the official ROS 2 Jazzy instructions to install ROS 2. This guide uses ros-jazzy-desktop.

docs.title: Installing Tobas
docs.text:
Install Tobas from the ROS 2 apt repository.

$ sudo apt update
$ sudo apt install ros-jazzy-tobas

docs.title: What You Need
docs.text:
• Raspberry Pi 5 (2 GB or more)
  • A microSD card with at least 16 GB (e.g., SanDisk Extreme microSDXC™ UHS-I CARD - 32GB)
  • An SD card reader (e.g., SANDISK QuickFlow microSD Card Reader with USB-C)

docs.title: Procedure
docs.text:
Download the Tobas image file before proceeding.

Install an image flashing tool. For example, you can use:

  • balenaEtcher
  • Raspberry Pi Imager

Connect the SD card to your PC using the card reader.

Launch the flashing tool, select the downloaded image and the target SD card, and start flashing. The following screenshot shows balenaEtcher.

Once flashing completes successfully, remove the SD card from your PC.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: Installation is now complete. We recommend restarting your PC before proceeding so that the changes made during installation take effect. Next, use Tobas Bootmedia Config to configure the initial settings before booting.

docs.title: Starting and Stopping
docs.text:
Launch Tobas GCS, load tobas_f450.TBS, and open Simulation from the tool buttons.

Click Start to build the project and launch the simulation. The first launch takes longer because environment data needs to be downloaded. Startup time depends on the complexity of the environment and your network connection, but it usually takes no more than 10 minutes.

Use Dynamic Configurations to adjust environmental settings such as wind speed, and Commanders to send commands to the aircraft. You can also use mission planning, parameter tuning, and the other features introduced in Flight Test, just as with real hardware.

Click Terminate to stop the simulation.

docs.title: Control with an RC Transmitter
docs.text: You can control the simulated aircraft with an RC transmitter. The simulation uses the RC calibration results saved on your PC, so complete calibration on that PC before proceeding.

docs.title: Preparing a USB-to-Serial Module
docs.text: FTDI FT234X is one example of a suitable USB-to-serial module. Configure the module to invert the signal's high and low levels.

docs.title: Joining the dialout Group
docs.text:
To access USB serial devices, add your current user to the dialout group with the following command.

$ sudo usermod -aG dialout "${USER}"

Restart your PC after running the command for the change to take effect. You only need to do this once.

docs.title: Steps for Each Simulation Run
docs.text:
1. Connect the USB-to-serial module to your PC and RC receiver.
  2. Select your device in the S.BUS/Device field under Simulation Settings.
  3. Start the simulation. If transmitter signals appear in Control System, setup is successful and you can control the aircraft just as you would with real hardware.

docs.title: Control via ROS
docs.text: All communication between the flight controller's components uses ROS, so you can control the aircraft from your own programs. See User Code (Python) and User Code (C++) for details.

docs.title: Tobas ユーザガイド
docs.text: Tobasは，モデルベース設計とLinuxを基盤とした，ドローン・ロボット航空機向けフライトコントローラです． 従来のフライトコントローラと異なり，個々の機体の構造を詳細に考慮して制御系を設計するため， 従来のフライトコントローラでは難しい機体でも精度良く飛ばすことができます．

docs.title: 特徴
docs.text:
• 独自のフォーマットで機体構造を定義し，機体の構造を正しく制御器に反映
  • モータの回転数制御により，応答性・追従精度が向上
  • 可動ジョイントの角度変化による自重・反力を補償
  • 突風や地面効果などの外乱を補償
  • GUI 上で機体構成や制御パラメータを設定可能
  • ROS 2 に対応し，シミュレーションと実機で同じインターフェースを提供

docs.title: 制御性能の向上
docs.text:
Tobas はユーザの機体の物理特性を正しく利用して制御を行うため， 従来のフライトコントローラよりも優れた制御性能を発揮できます． 例えば以下のような情報を考慮しています．

  • 機体を構成する各剛体リンクの力学パラメータ: 質量，重心，慣性テンソル
  • バッテリーのスペック: セル数，放電容量，放電率
  • モータのスペック: KV 値，内部抵抗，磁極数
  • プロペラのスペック: 直径，ピッチ，推力定数，反トルク定数

docs.title: 機体設計の幅を拡大
docs.text:
Tobas では機体の構造はUADF (Universal Aircraft Description Format)で定義され， 従来のフライトコントローラでは難しかった様々な機体を飛ばすことができます． 例えば，Tobas は以下のような変則的な機体にも対応しています．

  • ペイロードにより重心が中心部から大きく外れた機体
  • カメラの画角を確保するためにプロペラの配置が非対称な機体
  • ロボットアームを搭載した機体
  • チルトロータを搭載した機体

docs.title: ゲイン調整の手間を削減
docs.text: 機体を正しくモデル化することで，並進系と回転系のダイナミクスを機体に非依存の形で取り出せ，事前に解析することができます． それにより Tobas では予め無難なゲインが設定されており，ユーザは基本的にゲイン調整をすることなく機体を飛ばすことができます． また，必要であれば全てのパラメータを飛行中にオンラインで調整することができます．

docs.title: 現実に即したシミュレーション
docs.text:
機体の質量特性や推進系の空力特性を考慮しているため，現実に即した物理シミュレーションが可能です． それにより，実機試験のコストを大幅に削減することができます．

以下のような，飛行に大きな影響を与える要素を簡単にシミュレーションできます：

  • 風 (定常風，乱流，突風)
  • バッテリーの電圧降下
  • ESC の最大電流
  • センサの遅延，ノイズ
  • 吊り下げ荷物

docs.title: クアッドコプター
docs.text: 典型的なクアッドコプターです． DJI F450 のフレームキットを使用しています．

docs.title: 非平面ロータ配置ヘキサコプター
docs.text: 全てのプロペラが水平面から 30 度傾いているヘキサコプターです． 平面ロータ配置のマルチコプターは位置を変化させるために姿勢を変化させる必要があるのに対し， 非平面ロータ配置マルチコプターは位置と姿勢を独立に制御することができます． そのため，地面と平行の姿勢を保ったまま平行移動したり，ホバリングしたまま姿勢を変化させることができます． また，直接水平方向に推力を発生させられるため位置決め精度が高く，耐風性能にも優れています．

docs.title: アクティブチルトヘキサコプター
docs.text: 全てのアームを両方向に 120 度ずつ回転させられるヘキサコプターです． ホバリングした状態で姿勢を大きく変化させられるのが特徴です． 取り付けた検査機器等を任意の姿勢で保持することができるため，例えば傾いた壁面に対する非破壊検査への応用が期待されます．

docs.title: ロボットアームドローン
docs.text: チルトヘキサコプターに 4 軸のロボットアームを搭載した機体です． アームにより発生する反力や重心の変化を動的に補償することで， アームを大きく振り回しても位置姿勢を一定範囲内に留めることができています．

docs.title: PC
docs.text:
以下の要件を満たす必要があります．

要件 必須 推奨 備考 OS Ubuntu 24.04 LTS (ROS 2 Jazzy) ネイティブ環境推奨 RAM 8GB 16GB CPU AMD64 (x86-64) GPU NVIDIA GeForce RTX ディスプレイ解像度 FHD (1080p) 4K UHD (2160p)

docs.title: ESC
docs.text:
Bidirectional DShot プロトコルに対応している必要があります． 例えば以下のファームウェアは対応しています．

  • BLHeli_32 (2024 年 6 月にサポート終了)
  • AM32
  • bluejay

docs.title: GNSS アンテナ
docs.text: FMU に搭載されている GNSS 受信機の周波数帯域とコネクタに対応している必要があります．

docs.title: RC 受信機
docs.text: 8 チャンネル以上の S.BUS に対応している必要があります．

docs.title: 3Dモデル
docs.text: 製品の 3D モデルです． 機体設計の際にご利用ください．

docs.title: 代表的な慣性モーメント
docs.text: 質量\(m\)の密度均一な物体の重心周りの慣性モーメントの求め方を紹介します． URDF を作る際にご利用ください．

docs.title: 3 辺の長さが\(x\)，\(y\)，\(z\)の直方体
半径\(r\)，高さ\(h\)の円柱
半径\(r\)の球
RPMフィルタとは
docs.text: RPMフィルタとは，モータの回転周波数とその高調波を中心周波数とするノッチフィルタです． ドローン，特にマルチコプターにおいて，IMUに生じる振動のほとんどはプロペラによるものなので， その回転数にノッチフィルタの中心周波数を追従させることで振動を効果的に除去することができます．

docs.title: RPMフィルタの効果
docs.text:
RPMフィルタを用いる最大の利点は，フィルタリング効果が非常に高いことです． ノッチフィルタの中心周波数におけるゲインはゼロであり，理想的には中心周波数の振動は完全に消滅します． 実際は中心周波数の誤差や離散化誤差により完全に振動が消えることはありませんが， それでもローパスフィルタに比べると遥かに高いフィルタリング効果を発揮します．

下の画像はF450を飛行させたときのIMUの時系列データと周波数解析結果です． 灰色が生のデータ，青色がフィルタリング後のデータです． 左列はカットオフ40HzのLPFのみを適用したとき，右列はRPMフィルタのみを適用したときです． LPFのみだと高周波は落とせてもモータ回転数の振動が強く残っているのに対し， RPMフィルタの場合はモータの回転周波数とその2，3倍周波の振動も大幅にカットできていることが分かります．

IMU，特にジャイロの振動が減少すると，モータの回転数の変動も減少します． 下の画像で青色が観測した回転数，赤色が目標の回転数ですが，ノッチフィルタを用いた場合の方が回転数の変動が小さいことが分かります． これにより，余計な力が働かないことで姿勢制御がより安定することに加え， モータの発熱量が減ったりプロペラの羽音が滑らかになるという効果も得られます．

docs.title: 対応FMU
docs.text:
以下のFMUではRPMフィルタを使用することができます．

  • FC2xx

docs.title: パラメータ
docs.text: GCSのParam TuningのIMU Filterの項でフィルタの設定を行うことができます． それぞれのパラメータの説明，初期値，調整方法を以下に記します．

docs.title: lowpass_filter/*_cutoff
docs.text: RPMフィルタとは別のローパスフィルタのカットオフ周波数です． 最初は3つ全て0Hzに設定してください．これでフィルタが無効化されます． RPMフィルタではモータ，プロペラ由来の振動以外は落とせないため，どうしても強い振動が残る場合は部分的にLPFを有効化してください．

docs.title: rpm_filter/quality_factor
docs.text: ノッチフィルタの鋭さを決める値です． 大きいほど鋭い（バンド幅が狭い）代わりに遅延が小さくなります． デフォルトは0でフィルタが無効になっています． 最初は遅延とバンド幅のバランスがとれた5に設定してください． 実際に飛ばしてみてFFTでピークが視認できないほどに振動がカットされていることが確認できたら， ピークが残る直前まで1つずつ値を大きくしてみてください．

docs.title: rpm_filter/min_center_frequency, rpm_filter/fade_range
docs.text:
RPMフィルタを適用する中心周波数の範囲に関するパラメータです． 前者を\(f_\mathrm{m}\)，後者を\(f_\mathrm{f}\)とすると，中心周波数\(f_\mathrm{c}\)に対してノッチフィルタは以下のように適用されます．

  • \(f_\mathrm{c} \lt f_\mathrm{m}\): フィルタ無効
  • \(f_\mathrm{m} \le f_\mathrm{c} \lt f_\mathrm{m} + f_\mathrm{f}\): 遷移領域（\(f_\mathrm{c}\)が大きいほどフィルタが強くなる）
  • \(f_\mathrm{m} + f_\mathrm{f} \le f_\mathrm{c}\): フィルタ有効

フィルタを無効化する領域を設けているのは，制御帯域に近い低周波側をフィルタリングすると応答性や安定性に悪影響が出る可能性があるためです． 遷移領域を設けているのは，RPMフィルタの有効・無効が切り替わった際に全体のフィルタ特性が急激に変化するのを避けるためです． ホバリング回転周波数\(f_\mathrm{h}\)に対し， 最初は\(f_\mathrm{m}=\frac{f_\mathrm{h}}{2}\)，\(f_\mathrm{f}=\frac{f_\mathrm{h}}{4}\)程度に設定してください．

docs.title: rpm_filter/lpf_cutoff
docs.text: RPMフィルタの中心周波数にかけるローパスフィルタのカットオフ周波数です． ESCから得られるモータの回転数は変動が大きく，そのまま中心周波数として使用するとフィルタ特性の変動が大きすぎるため平滑化しています． 多くの場合デフォルトのままで問題ありません．

docs.title: システム構成
docs.text: Tobas の大まかなシステム構成について，ハードウェアとソフトウェアに分けて説明します．

docs.title: ハードウェア構成
docs.text: 下図はハードウェアの構成図です． HAT からシリアル通信で送られたセンサデータは，RPi 上のハードウェア仮想化層 (Hardware Abstraction Layer, 以下 HAL) で共通の ROS メッセージに変換された後 CPU1-3 で動作するフライトコードで処理されます． フライトコードから出力された目標モータ回転数は再び HAL を通過した後 HAT 上のモータ速度制御用 MCU に送られ， 計算されたスロットルはデジタル通信で ESC に指示されます． CPU0 では遠隔通信のためのインターフェースノードがフライトコードとは別のプロセスで動作しており， 地上局などリモートからフライトコントローラにアクセスする際は必ずこのノードを通過します． このように通信に関する処理のプロセスとコアを分離しているのは，フライトコードのリアルタイム性を確保し，予期せぬ動作を防ぐためです．

docs.title: ソフトウェア構成
docs.text: 下図はソフトウェアの構成図です． 実機もしくは Gazebo 上の機体からのセンサデータは HAL で共通の ROS メッセージに変換されます． センサデータは状態推定器に送られ，機体の位置，姿勢，速度，角速度が推定されます． 推定された状態は図の二重枠で囲まれた制御器に送られ，各プロペラの目標推力が計算されます． 目標推力からプロペラのモデルに従ってモータの目標回転数が計算されます． 目標回転数は再び HAL を通過した後，実機もしくは Gazebo 上の機体に指令されます． 実機の場合，目標回転数から MCU 上のモータ制御器でモータへの印加電圧が計算され，ESC に送信されます． 飛行制御器やモータ制御器に必要な機体の物理モデルは，Setup Assistantで作成した Tobas プロジェクトから取得します．

docs.title: トラブルシューティング
docs.text: 現在までに報告されたトラブルとその解決方法をまとめています．

docs.title: 1. ディスプレイサーバが X11 になっていない可能性
docs.text:
Settings / System / About / System Details から，ディスプレイサーバが X11 になっていることを確認してください．

もしも X11 でない場合，例えば Wayland と表示されている場合は， Ubuntu の起動画面でユーザ名を選択した際に画面右下に現れる歯車から，ディスプレイサーバを以下のように選択してください．

  • Ubuntu もしくは Ubuntu on Wayland が選択可能な場合 → Ubuntu
  • Ubuntu on Xorg もしくは Ubuntu が選択可能な場合 → Ubuntu on Xorg

docs.title: FC と PC 間の ROS 通信ができない
1. ファイアウォールがUDPを弾いている可能性
docs.text:
ROS 2 のネットワーク間通信は内部で UDP を用いていますが， ファイアウォールがそれを許可していない可能性があります． 以下のコマンドでファイアウォールの状態を確認し， 許可されたポートリストに UDP の 7400 台のポートが含まれなければこれが原因かもしれません．

$ sudo ufw status

本当は使用するポートのみを許可するのが望ましいですが， ひとまずUFWを無効化して再起動すると通信できるようになります．

$ sudo ufw disable
$ sudo reboot

docs.title: ユーザコードを作成して書き込んだが FC が動作していない
docs.text:
ランタイムエラーが発生している可能性があります． SSH でラズパイにログインし，journalctlでコンソール出力を確認すると手がかりが掴めるかもしれません． 十字キーで移動し，Qキーで終了できます．

$ ssh pi@${hostname}.local  # or pi@${ip_address}
$ journalctl -u tobas_real_realtime.service -e  # or tobas_real_interface.service

docs.title: UADFとは
docs.text: Tobas が定義している Universal Aircraft Description Format (UADF) とは， ロボットを表現する一般的なフォーマットである Universal Robot Description Format (URDF) に， 飛翔体特有の要素を追加したフォーマットです．

docs.title: URDF とは
docs.text: 剛体リンク系で表現されるあらゆるロボットを記述するためのフォーマットです． ロボットに含まれる各リンクの質量情報，接触情報，視覚情報に加え，それらをつなぐジョイントが定義されます． 詳しくはurdf | ROS.orgをご参照ください．

docs.title: UADF と URDF の違い
docs.text: UADF では，URDF のジョイント型に加えて，飛翔体特有の以下のジョイント型が追加されています．

docs.title: thrust
docs.text:
モータ，プロペラを合わせた推進ユニットを表すジョイントです． URDF のcontinuousがベースですが，以下の点が異なります．

  • axis: 回転軸．軸方向に推力が出る想定．
  • direction: 回転方向．valueにcwまたはccwを指定する．

Note

thrustジョイントはエンドジョイントでなければなりません．

docs.title: cs
docs.text:
固定翼機の操舵面 (Control Surface) を表すジョイントです． URDF のrevoluteがベースになっています．

Note

csジョイントはエンドジョイントでなければなりません．

docs.title: tilt
docs.text:
アクティブチルトロータのチルトジョイントを表します． URDF のrevoluteがベースになっています．

Note

tiltジョイントの先には 1 つのthrustジョイントが接続していなければなりません．

docs.title: UADF の作成方法
docs.text:
ここでは，チュートリアルで用いた典型的なクアッドコプターである DJI F450 の UADF を作成します．

URDF には視覚化のためにメッシュファイルやテクスチャファイルを取り込む機能があり， URDF そのものに加えてそれらのファイルも一緒に配布されることが多いため， ロボットごとに専用の ROS パッケージを作ると便利です． 今回は ~/colcon_ws/src/ 直下にtobas_f450_description というパッケージを作成し，その中に必要な全てのファイルを含めることにします． TobasFlightControl/tobas_f450_description に完成したパッケージを公開しています．

docs.title: ROS パッケージの構成と必須ファイル
docs.text:
tobas_f450_descriptionは以下のような構成になっています．

tobas_f450_description/
├── meshes
│   ├── frame.stl
│   ├── phantom3_0945_ccw.stl
│   ├── phantom3_0945_cw.stl
│   └── tobas_fc100.stl
├── urdf
│   └── f450.uadf
├── CMakeLists.txt
└── package.xml

package.xmlはパッケージの概要と依存関係を記述したファイルです． 各 ROS パッケージのルートに必ず 1 つ置く必要があります． 今回作るパッケージは外部のパッケージには依存していないため，パッケージ名やライセンスなど最小限の要素のみ記述しています．

<package format="3">
    <name>tobas_f450_description</name>
    <version>0.0.0</version>
    <description>A UADF example for the DJI F450.</description>
    <maintainer email="m.dohi@tobas.jp">Masayoshi Dohi</maintainer>
    <license>MIT</license>
    <buildtool_depend>ament_cmake</buildtool_depend>
    <export>
        <build_type>ament_cmake</build_type>
    </export>
</package>

CMakeLists.txtはパッケージのビルドやインストールの手順を記述したファイルです． メッシュファイルを格納するディレクトリであるmeshesと，UADF を格納するディレクトリであるurdfをインストールするようにします．

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.25)
project(tobas_f450_description)
find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
install(DIRECTORY meshes urdf DESTINATION share/${PROJECT_NAME})
ament_package()

docs.title: UADF の書き方
docs.text:
今回作成する F450 の UADF は以下のような構成要素から成ります．

  • 空のルートリンク (必須)
  • モータを含むメインフレーム
  • メインフレームに固定されたバッテリー
  • メインフレームに固定された FMU
  • 4 つのプロペラ

これらの要素はそれぞれ 1 つの剛体リンクとして記述され， それらが適切なジョイントで接続されることで全体として 1 つのツリー構造を形成します．

今回はメインフレーム以下の全てのリンクをルートリンクにぶら下げる形をとることにします． 全体のツリー構造は以下のようになります．

base_link
├──frame
├──battery
├──fmu
├──propeller_0
├──propeller_1
├──propeller_2
└──propeller_3

まず，URDF のルート要素を記述します． URDF のルート要素はrobotでなければならず，name属性を指定する必要があります． 以下の全ての要素はこのルート要素の中に記述します．

<robot name="f450">
</robot>

robotの中に空のルートリンクを記述します． ルートリンクは大きさや質量を持たない概念上のリンクで，全ての UADF は必ず 1 つのルートリンクを持つ必要があります．

  <!-- Base Link (Empty) -->
  <link name="base_link"/>

メインフレームをルートリンクに固定します． visualのメッシュファイルはパッケージからの相対パスで指定しています． このようにpackage://<package name>で ROS パッケージへの相対パスを記述できます． collisionの接触領域はメッシュファイルを使うとシミュレーションが重くなるため直方体で近似しています． inertialの質量特性は 3D CAD から取得した値をそのまま転記しています．

  <!-- Main Frame -->
  <joint name="frame_joint" type="fixed">
    <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <parent link="base_link"/>
    <child link="frame"/>
  </joint>
  <link name="frame">
    <inertial>
      <mass value="0.55346"/>
      <origin xyz="0 0 -0.004136" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <inertia ixx="0.008128" ixy="0" ixz="0" iyy="0.008193" iyz="0" izz="0.01597"/>
    </inertial>
    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <mesh filename="package://tobas_f450_description/meshes/frame.stl" scale="1 1 1"/>
      </geometry>
      <material name="black">
        <color rgba="0 0 0 1"/>
      </material>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 -0.03" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.35 0.35 0.06"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>

バッテリーと FMU をメインフレームと同じ要領で追加します． それぞれの慣性モーメントは，質量がcollisionと同じ大きさの直方体に均一に分布している場合の値を計算して記入しています． 具体的な計算方法についてはInertia Momentをご確認ください．

  <!-- Battery -->
  <joint name="battery_joint" type="fixed">
    <origin xyz="0 0 -0.025" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <parent link="base_link"/>
    <child link="battery"/>
  </joint>
  <link name="battery">
    <inertial>
      <mass value="0.376"/>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <inertia ixx="9.024e-05" ixy="0" ixz="0" iyy="0.000770831" iyz="0" izz="0.000824975"/>
    </inertial>
    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.155 0.048 0.024"/>
      </geometry>
      <material name="yellow">
        <color rgba="1 1 0 1"/>
      </material>
    </visual>
    <collision>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <geometry>
        <box size="0.155 0.048 0.024"/>
      </geometry>
    </collision>
  </link>

  <!-- Flight Management Unit -->
  <joint name="fmu_joint" type="fixed">
    <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>
    <parent link="base_link"/>
    <child link="fmu"/>
  </joint>
  <link name="fmu">
    <inertial>
      <mass value="0.16"/>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0.014" rpy="0 0 0"/>
      <inertia ixx="6.17067e-05" ixy="0" ixz="0" iyy="0.000118453" iyz="0" izz="0.000159253"/>
    </inertial>
    <visual>
      <origin xyz="0 0 0" rpy="0 0 0"/>

プロペラを追加します． ジョイントタイプに UADF 特有のthrustを指定し，axisを推力方向の+Z 軸方向 (0 0 1)，directionを反時計回り (ccw) とします． visualのメッシュファイルはパッケージからの相対パスで指定しています． collisionの接触領域は円柱で近似しています． inertialの慣性モーメントは，質量がcollisionと同じ大きさの円柱に均一に分布している場合の値を計算して記入しています． 具体的な計算方法についてはInertia Momentをご確認ください．
